keep.brief: Jarmen Kell (GLA, T3, Barracks plus Palace): cover his rifle; the button snipe that kills a vehicle's crew so the empty hull goes neutral for any soldier to claim (hijack-vehicle; the claiming itself is game-wide), with riders thrown out of a sniped transport; camouflage until he fires (cloak); the one-at-a-time limit; that vehicles cannot crush him; and uncrewed machines such as the Sentry Drone as the hard counter. Juhziz's demo charges go in notes.
keep.why: The batch's only crew snipe and the registry's own hijack-vehicle example, and the first marksman primary in the data. He sets up a teammate's steal, and the kept Sentry Drone is his built-in counter. He is also the opening-check unit for Generals.

keep.brief: Battle Bus (GLA, T3, Arms Dealer plus Palace): cover the eight seats whose riders shoot out of it (passenger-sets-weapon, fire-port variant); its second life when the hull dies, a parked bunker with fresh health whose riders survive hurt and keep shooting until it falls; that getting out ends the bunker; the salvage armour step in notes; that it never ranks up; and the 1.03 change that stops Hijackers while anyone rides. Check which on_death term, if any, fits the bunker.
keep.why: The batch's clearest new death rule: the enemy has to kill it twice, and a full load gets a last stand. Its fire-port seats repeat the IFV sample, so the death bunker is what it adds.

keep.brief: Technical (GLA, T1, Arms Dealer): cover the machine gun and the two salvage steps (a splash cannon, then a rocket launcher that point-defence lasers can stop), each recorded as an acquired weapon plus one triggered ability linking leech-weapon-on-kill, as the Generals notes say; that only GLA units see the crates and a dead GLA vehicle drops one too; its very high speed; and the open bed for five riders, who survive its death hurt. Juhziz's higher price goes in notes.
keep.why: Scavenging as a fixed upgrade ladder: drive over scrap to move the gun up, so a good driver snowballs. It twists the RA3 Hammer Tank's leech (a set ladder, shared crates) and is the batch's cheap t1 raider.

keep.brief: Overlord (China, T3, War Factory plus Propaganda Center): cover the twin cannons on the turret; running over enemy vehicles; and the single add-on bought in the field, one of three (a bunker for five shooters, a Gattling cannon that hits aircraft and infantry and spots stealth, a propaganda tower that heals it and nearby allies and speeds their fire), as upgrade-in-field, rally-allies, repair-allies and passenger-sets-weapon. Tao's faster, irradiating version and the generals who lack it go in notes.
keep.why: The registry's own example for upgrade-in-field and rally-allies: a super-heavy whose player picks a job partway through a life (anti-air gunner, rolling bunker or healing aura). The add-on choice is its twist over the RA1 Mammoth Tank.

keep.brief: Red Guard (China, T1, Barracks): cover the pair of riflemen trained together; the horde bonus (horde units fire faster while five or more stand together) as an innate passive with no pattern and a fit_note, as the Generals notes say; the Capture Building upgrade (capture-structure, source upgrade); and splash on the clump, such as flash-bangs, as the counter. Shin Fai's Mini-Gunner goes in notes.
keep.why: Strength in numbers with no leader: a team bonus that switches off when the group thins or splits. It is the batch's only group-size passive and its cheapest unit.

keep.brief: Hacker (China, T3, Barracks plus Propaganda Center): cover the laptop that earns cash for his side while he stays set up, with income that rises as he ranks up from hacking (said in the ability summary, as the notes ask); the short-range hack that shuts an enemy building down while he keeps at it (capture-structure, sabotage variant); and that he is unarmed and fragile. Shin Fai's camouflaged Super Hacker goes in notes.
keep.why: Money from nothing: the batch's economy player, who earns with no resource node or delivery route and pays back more the longer he lives, so the enemy team must hunt him.

keep.brief: Aurora Bomber (USA, T3, Air Field plus Strategy Center): cover the supersonic run on which nothing can hit it; the one heavy bomb that cannot be jammed or shot down and does not follow a moving target; the slow, exposed trip home and the reload on a landing pad (jet, high air); and Granger's Fuel-Air and Alexander's Aurora Alpha versions in notes. Check whether become-invulnerable fits the run.
keep.why: Commitment as armour: a high-air jet that is untouchable on its run and helpless after it, so the counter is timing. No researched unit ties immunity to an attack run.

keep.brief: Sentry Drone (USA, T1, War Factory): cover the uncrewed body that crew snipes, Hijackers and neutron shells cannot touch (an immunity, with Jarmen Kell as a foiled enemy); camouflage while it stands still and holds fire (cloak); stealth detection around it (sensors); the optional gun bought in the field (upgrade-in-field); and that it never ranks up.
keep.why: The batch's only drone-class unit and its cleanest iconic counter: a parked, hidden watcher that exposes stealth and turns the GLA's crew-killing tricks around. Uncrewed like the RA2 Robot Tank, but immune to crew kills rather than mind control.

keep.brief: Combat Chinook (USA Air Force General, T1, Supply Center once a War Factory stands): cover the eight seats for infantry or vehicles; riders shooting from its ports (passenger-sets-weapon); the point-defence laser against missiles (an armour model, not a pattern); supply runs (gather-resources, not while it carries anyone); and Combat Drop, which ropes Rangers into a building (drop-in-from-above). Check on https://cnc.fandom.com/wiki/Combat_Chinook what the drop does to a building the enemy holds.
keep.why: A low-air flying multitool that switches between supply runs and an assault taxi; its rope drop is the batch's passenger-delivery case of drop-in-from-above. As the Air Force General's own unit it also covers a Generals subfaction.

keep.brief: Drone Operator (GDF, T1, Barracks): cover his anti-tank pistol; the drone's small missiles at ground and air targets his side can already see; the toggle that roots him and hands him the drone on a leash; the toggle that sends it back to follow; the drone's replacement and its death with him; and the drone fighting on outside while he rides or garrisons (launch-drones, piloted variant). The Combat Drone page says the drones cannot be steered, which clashes with his toggle, and patch 2.0.0 made him a little faster.
keep.why: A pet drone you fly yourself on a short leash: the batch's launch-drones unit and the RA3 Terror Drone turned around (a drone you own, not one you are). It scouts cliffs and keeps fighting while its owner rides with a teammate.

keep.brief: Sentinel (GDF, T1, Vehicle Bay): cover the minigun that hits ground and air and, in multiplayer, marks its main target (weapon trait mark); the scanner-round toggle that marks every enemy around the one hit for little damage (switch-weapon-mode); what Marked does (more range and damage from GDF Networked weapons, Intel paid when the target dies); its very high speed and long sight; and its thin health. The page was last checked at 1.6.0, so read the patches since.
keep.why: A scout that trades damage for team-wide tagging: its tags make heavier teammates hit harder and pay the team on each kill. It twists switch-weapon-mode (damage against tagging) and is a scout primary, which the data lacks.

keep.brief: Shieldmaiden (GDF, T2, Satellite Uplink with Specialist Pod, built at the Vehicle Bay): cover the field that, while it stands still, slows every enemy rocket and missile weapon inside it to half rate (Missile Interference); the Intel-paid repair turret that mends allied vehicles nearby (deploy-turret, repair-allies); the long-range laser that hits only aircraft; hover rules (sets off no mines, neither crushes nor is crushed); and its Intel price at the registry's rate.
keep.why: A protector that bends the fight: the batch's only anti-missile field and its anti-air primary, plus a placed repair turret (deploy-turret). It stands in for Generals' ECM Tank, whose missile field teaches the same thing.

keep.brief: Line Officer (Dynasty, T2, Specialist Bureau): cover Inspire Troops (nearby infantry briefly move and fire faster: rally-allies); Supervise Crew (he boards a friendly vehicle, one officer each, which turns Elite while he rides, and he is thrown clear alive if it dies); what Elite gives per the Veterancy page; and his slow, heavy pistol. The page was checked at 1.4.0 and 2.0.0 gave the pistol more range, so read the patches between.
keep.why: A rider who makes a teammate's tank elite instead of arming it: a seat-synergy lesson no researched unit has, beyond the IFV sample's rider-sets-the-gun. Also the batch's on-key rally and a buffer primary.

keep.brief: Voltaic Tank (Dynasty, T3, Defender upgrade, built at the Machine Shop): cover the beam that charges before each shot, jumps between packed vehicles and destroys any vehicle already in Tempest Overflow (execute-target); how allied weapons stack Tempest Charge up to Overflow; the short shutdown of defences it hits and its weak damage to buildings; and the Martial Plan trade of health for fire rate (overclock-self). https://tempestrising.wiki.gg/wiki/Tempest_Overflow leaves it out of the finisher list, so settle that conflict.
keep.why: The closer of a team combo: teammates build the overload, it finishes the target. The kill depends on a state others build up, a twist on the RA1 Attack Dog's execute-target and the RA3 Cryocopter's freeze-and-shatter.

keep.brief: Tempest Sphere (Dynasty, T3, Defender upgrade, built at the Machine Shop): cover crushing everything smaller than itself (hover units and heavy vehicles escape); ramming bigger targets and the multiplayer Vulnerability that follows; the long-cooldown straight-line charge (dash); Tempest Plating, which turns Tempest Charge into repairs; the Demolitionist it leaves when destroyed; and its rolling ball body, for which the mobility and body lists have no term (record the gap).
keep.why: The batch's odd one: a giant rolling wrecking ball that heals from a debuff that slows other vehicles and leaves a heavy trooper behind. It brings dash and a crush-by-size rule no researched unit has.

keep.brief: Enlightened (Veti, T1, appears free at the Resurrection Anchor; also from the Corral, Ambassador captures and Subjugated kills): cover its weak brawl attack; the key that sacrifices it to give allied units and buildings around it Consecration (less damage taken, more speed) plus a perk by receiver (reload, repair, a summoned Servitor, sight and detection, income) as rally-allies and resupply-allies; its use as fuel for Caretakers and Luminaries; the 2.0.0 changes; and that it is never bought (cost_band allows null only for games with no purchases, so record the gap).
keep.why: A free unit whose real job is to die well for its team: the first researched unit that spends itself to help allies rather than to hurt enemies (the RA1 M.A.D. Tank and RA3 Terror Drone hurt). It also brings resupply-allies.

keep.brief: Thunderhead (Veti, T2, Veti Eye with Initial Awakening, built at the Celestial Gate): cover that it is unarmed; the Lightning Rod it drops, a fortified pylon that soldiers and tanks walk into; the recall that dissolves the Rod and teleports everyone inside to the aircraft (build-linked-exits, teleport, carry-passengers); the Arcing zap at close attackers (that page gives two damage figures); its air layer; and the 2.0.0 rise in health and speed. Its page is unverified.
keep.why: A transport that never takes anyone aboard: it carries a linked exit, so it is the batch's only build-linked-exits unit (the Generals tunnel example is a structure). It also brings the zap-back passive.

keep.brief: Vimana (Veti, T3, Veti Eye with Transcendent Awakening, built at the Celestial Gate, one per Gate): cover Gate Link (aircraft its Gate builds appear beside it: host-spawn-point); teleporting anywhere inside its owner's build area; the summoned Caretakers with Combat Servitors; the paid area Consecration (rally-allies); the Subjugation aura; the cannon that ignores resistances (Omni damage has no damage_map key); and its instant death when its Gate falls (depend-on-relay). The gate conflict and the unverified page need the 2.0.0 notes.
keep.why: A flying fortress that is the team's forward spawn and dies the moment its home Gate falls: the batch's only host-spawn-point unit, and a harsher depend-on-relay than the RA2 Robot Tank, which only shuts down. It also carries the batch's convert-on-kill aura.

keep.brief: Anna Kos and Wojtek (Polania, hero; take her gate and tier from the Iron Harvest notes, Headquarters or Reserve): cover her long rifle; the aimed shot that passes through every target on its line (fire-power-shot); the bear that brawls when sent, comes back when recalled and slowly heals nearby friendly soldiers, walking over to hurt ones (repair-allies); the bear as one lasting AI partner; and the knock-out and free revive of heroes from the notes.
keep.why: A hero split into a frail sniper and a bear that is bodyguard and medic at once, with a piercing shot that rewards lining targets up. It brings fire-power-shot and, with Olga, the companion lesson no registry id covers.

keep.brief: PZM-13 'Mocny' (Polania, T2, Advanced Workshop): cover its two modes, walking (direct cannon fire and smoke that keeps surrounding it as it moves) and planted (a longer, harder cannon and a smoke shell that leaves a fixed screen where it lands), as deploy-siege-mode and lay-smoke; the DevBlog #45 price; its rear damage, where its page and Changelog #06 disagree (follow the notes); and its in-game name.
keep.why: The batch's smoke unit, whose support tool changes with its deploy mode. It gives lay-smoke its first researched unit.

keep.brief: Sd. KS 49 'Grimbart' (Saxony, T1, Saxon Workshop): cover the gatling; the key sweep that roots it and fires across an arc the player sizes, a wider arc holding it in place longer (suppress-with-fire); DevBlog #35's change that made its normal gun suppress too and the sweep pin harder; its Reserve II listing; and anti-mech guns as its counter.
keep.why: An on-key suppression with a clear trade between width and time spent rooted: the first researched suppress-with-fire, in the button form the registry asks for.

keep.brief: SKS 300 'Kaiser' (Saxony, T3, Advanced Workshop and Advanced Barracks, never from the Reserve): cover the main cannon fixed to the front, so the whole machine turns to aim; the ball-mounted flank machine guns that fire on the move; Entrench (it roots, raises the cannon and opens rocket launchers that cover all round except behind) as deploy-siege-mode; the rear weak spot; crushing houses as the game-wide rule; and field guns and flankers as counters.
keep.why: The batch's top-tier walker and Iron Harvest's only t3: it sets the ceiling for walker size, tier and price, and its fixed cannon makes the body the aim. It is also the opening-check unit for Iron Harvest.

keep.brief: Olga Morozova and Changa (Rusviet, hero; gate and tier from the notes; her page is titled Olga Romanova): cover stealth that holds until an enemy comes near or she acts and returns once none is close (cloak); remote charges stuck on mechs or buildings that go off when she walks out of range (throw-explosive); calling and riding the tiger for speed, visible while mounted (transform); the tiger fighting briefly when an attack drops her off; and her price from the DevBlogs.
keep.why: A stealth saboteur with a walk-away detonation and an animal mount: cloak by distance rather than stillness, and the second companion hero, whose partner is also her mount.

keep.brief: SHM-68 'Nakovalnya' (Rusviet, T1, Rusviet Workshop): cover the rocket barrage aimed by hand at an area with no set-up (bombard-area); Sentry Mode, a veteran ability that anchors it and fires single rockets by itself at anything entering a small chosen zone (deploy-siege-mode, zone-anchor variant, source veterancy); its class by how it moves (two big wheels pushed by small legs, though the game calls it a mech); rear damage per the notes; and its weakness up close.
keep.why: A placed kill-zone that fires on its own: the first source unit for deploy-siege-mode's zone-anchor variant, plus a hand-aimed barrage and the batch's odd wheel-and-leg body.

keep.brief: William Mason (Usonia, hero; gate and tier from the notes): cover the exosuit's burst cannon; climbing out and leaving the suit as a fixed turret while he runs with a revolver (deploy-turret); ordering the empty suit to rocket-jump back to him (transform); the automatic eject before the suit is wrecked (on_death pilot-eject); calling a new suit to crash down at a spot he picks after a cooldown (drop-in-from-above); the suit's armour per the notes; and his class (power-suit infantry or walker).
keep.why: A pilot and his suit as two bodies: the machine fights on without him, and he can eject, recall and replace it. No researched unit splits pilot and machine.

keep.brief: M-22 'Stark' (Usonia, T2, Usonian Advanced Workshop): cover the pneumatic jackhammer for mechs and the side flamethrower for infantry, both used on the move; Berserk (more damage the more hurt it is); the key that shuts it down for a few seconds to patch itself, helpless meanwhile (heal-self); and Lech Kos's matching rage in notes.
keep.why: A health bar to play: it hits hardest when nearly dead and picks the moment for a short, exposed repair. It brings heal-self and the low-health rage, which no researched unit has.

keep.brief: Engineer squad (shared, T1, any faction's Headquarters, Barracks or Advanced Barracks): cover sandbags and barbed wire (build-cover); anti-armour mines (lay-mines); repairing mechs and buildings (repair-allies); building base structures; its weak gun; and its place as the stock crew of weapon systems. Record it once under shared, as the weapon systems are, name each faction's version in notes, and flag that the shared faction's registry note names only aircraft and weapon systems.
keep.why: The builder: the batch's only build-cover unit and the first engineer primary in the data. Every faction's engineer works the same way, so it is kept once.

cut.reason: Its garrison-flushing spray is a counter to buildings that many Generals units share and that may suit a weapon trait better, so clear-garrison is not proposed from this batch; its toxin damage repeats the RA2 Desolator, it is one general's basic soldier only, and the wiki and the 1.04 tooltip disagree on its matchup.

Its always-on missile-scrambling field teaches the same protector lesson as the kept Shieldmaiden, which adds a repair turret, and its vehicle-locking beam is disable-machine, already on the RA3 Terror Drone. First swap back if the merge pass wants deflect-missiles as an id of its own.

Its target designator is the weapon trait mark, which the kept Sentinel carries together with an ammo toggle and a kill bounty; its point-defence lasers are the interceptor armour model the kept Combat Chinook also has; its bought drone is launch-drones, covered by the kept Drone Operator; and it cannot hurt ground units.

Its heal and repair aura is repair-allies (the RA1 Field Mechanic, and the kept Overlord tower, Shieldmaiden turret, bear and Engineer), its seats are the Sudden Transport's carry-passengers, and its new cleanse lesson answers ground hazards that no kept unit lays. First swap if the generator needs an answer to leave-hazard-zone.

Stealth on a strike jet repeats cloak, already on three kept units, and the Aurora Bomber is the kept Generals jet; its Bunker Busters carry the same garrison-clearing idea as the cut Toxin Rebel. Cutting it leaves Generals without a t2 unit, a tier only promotions give there.

A stealthed marksman repeats the kept Jarmen Kell (camouflaged sniper) and Olga Morozova (cloak), and its sprint is dash, on the kept Tempest Sphere. Its stronger opening shot from stealth can become a cloak variant in the merge pass.

Timed, paid takeover of vehicles is mind-control, which the RA2 Mastermind already links, and taking enemy vehicles is the kept Jarmen Kell's lesson; its stealth repeats cloak, and the sources disagree on what kind it is.

Its pulse joins two ids the data already has (the RA1 Spy's reveal-area and the RA3 Terror Drone's disable-machine); the kept Shieldmaiden is the batch's anti-air primary; rearming at a pad repeats the RA1 Yak and the kept Aurora; and the kept Sentry Drone and Overlord already counter stealth.

Its raise-the-dead tag is carried by the kept Vimana's Subjugation aura, and its thrall-sacrifice reload is the Veti-wide Sacrificial Summons button, which the notes treat as faction-wide; the kept Enlightened teaches the other half of that loop.

Its top-tier weight is taught by the kept Kaiser and Overlord, its zap-back by the kept Thunderhead and its missile rain by bombard-area (Boris, the Spy, the kept Nakovalnya). The one-per-player cap, immunity to every debuff and missing anti-air are availability, immunity and counter facts, not new mechanics. First swap if the batch wants a Tempest Rising walker.

Riders who speed up the host's own guns are passenger-sets-weapon (the IFV sample and the kept Battle Bus, Overlord and Combat Chinook); its single heavy shell is fire-power-shot, on the kept Anna Kos; self-repair while still is an armour model like the RA1 Mammoth Tank's; and the Kaiser is the kept super-heavy walker.

Its landing strike is leap, on the RA3 Sickle; suits falling from the sky are drop-in-from-above, on the kept William Mason and Combat Chinook; field reinforcement is reinforce-squad (the RA2 Slave Miner); and the hero Lev Zubov shares the jump.

Its bomb drones are the drone-launcher weapon family, as on the RA2 Aircraft Carrier, not launch-drones; free rebuilding of followers is reinforce-squad (the Slave Miner) and the paid hurry is a small twist; high air is covered by the Aurora Bomber and the RA3 Kirov; and its gate is still in doubt.

Its set-up gun with a narrow arc is deploy-siege-mode (siege-gun variant, also on the kept Mocny) with a limited-arc mount, and the notes make crew loss and the taking over of abandoned weapon systems game-wide, so no lesson of its own stays on the unit. First swap for a crew-served gun or an Iron Harvest anti-armour primary.
A plain cheap flyer with no button: its lesson is a price and tier point, not a mechanic. The batch already has aircraft in both air layers, and its main prey, the Samson, is cut.

opening_reason: Required: git log ef62f3a..HEAD over data/vocab, schemas and the two scripts prints 9fda853 (word lists 1.1.0) and 8366649, so the rules changed after R1's agreement report. Jarmen Kell (Generals) and the Kaiser (Iron Harvest) come from two of the batch's games, an infantry hero and a super-heavy walker, and neither needs a new pattern (hijack-vehicle and cloak; deploy-siege-mode), so a split points at the word lists or the new notes. Kell tests the 1.1.0 role rules on official text (his 1.04 tooltip names infantry and vehicles, but the vehicle part comes from his snipe, not his rifle: rule-fix items 18 and 30), the soldier armour tie-break against Generals' infantry armour sets, the new availability and immune link kinds (one at a time, vehicles cannot crush him, uncrewed drones shrug off his snipe) and the cooldown band of a button snipe. The Kaiser tests the mount tie-break (a cannon fixed to the front, ball-mounted flank guns, rockets that open only when dug in), the size rule in a game with no tanks, Iron Harvest's shifted armour map and rear damage, a mode switch with no cooldown band, and the deploy variant. Together they try the Generals tooltip role lines and Iron Harvest's first game-wide list. Coder briefs, name only: 'SKS 300 Kaiser (Saxony, Iron Harvest)' and 'Jarmen Kell (GLA, Command & Conquer: Generals Zero Hour)'.
coverage: KEPT: 27 units, 9 per game (Generals, Tempest Rising, Iron Harvest); none of these games had a researched unit before. CLASSES: infantry 10 (Kell, Red Guard, Hacker, Drone Operator, Line Officer, Enlightened, Anna Kos, Olga, William Mason, Engineer); vehicles 7 (Battle Bus, Technical, Overlord, Sentinel, Voltaic Tank, Tempest Sphere, Nakovalnya); walkers 4 (Mocny, Grimbart, Kaiser, Stark); hover 1 (Shieldmaiden); drone 1 (Sentry Drone); aircraft 4: high air Aurora Bomber (jet), low air Combat Chinook (rotor), and the Thunderhead and Vimana, whose layer the researcher settles (Tempest Rising gives every flier one Flying move type; the slow Vimana reads as an airship, the Thunderhead as hovering flight). No ships: none of the three games builds naval units in skirmish. Odd ones: the rolling Sphere, the wheel-and-leg Nakovalnya, the free Enlightened, the unarmed Hacker and Thunderhead, the two-body Mason and two hero-and-animal pairs. FACTIONS: Generals GLA 3, China 3, USA 3 (the Combat Chinook under usa-air-force; the Toxin General's own unit is cut); Tempest Rising GDF 3, Dynasty 3, Veti 3; Iron Harvest Polania 2, Saxony 2, Rusviet 2, Usonia 2, shared 1 (the Engineer, kept once like the weapon systems). TIERS: t1 10, t2 5 (Shieldmaiden, Line Officer, Thunderhead, Mocny, Stark), t3 9, plus three Iron Harvest heroes whose tier follows the notes (Headquarters or Reserve). Generals has no t2, which only promotions give there. PRICE BANDS: very low 4 (Red Guard pair, Drone Operator, Anna Kos, Engineer), low 7, medium 3 (Battle Bus, Sentry Drone, Mason), high 5 (Combat Chinook, Shieldmaiden by Intel, Line Officer, Voltaic Tank, Kaiser), very high 6 (Kell, Overlord, Aurora, Sphere, Thunderhead, Vimana); the Enlightened is never bought and Olga's price needs the DevBlogs. Tempest Rising keeps no medium unit (the Riot Van is the swap if that matters). ROLES (primary guesses): assault 6, siege 3 (Aurora, Mocny, Nakovalnya), transport 3 (Battle Bus, Combat Chinook, Thunderhead), marksman 2 (Kell, Anna), scout 2 (Sentry Drone, Sentinel), anti-infantry 2 (Red Guard, Grimbart), anti-armour 2 (Drone Operator, Voltaic), buffer 2 (Line Officer, Enlightened), and one each of raider (Technical), logistics (Hacker), anti-air (Shieldmaiden), infiltrator (Olga) and engineer (Engineer). Marksman, scout and engineer are the data's first primaries of their kind; support, disabler and area-denial appear only as secondaries here and are already primaries in the data. REGISTRY IDS: the kept units link 33 ids, 16 of them new to the data: hijack-vehicle, cloak, upgrade-in-field, rally-allies, drop-in-from-above, launch-drones, deploy-turret, dash, resupply-allies, build-linked-exits, host-spawn-point, fire-power-shot, lay-smoke, suppress-with-fire, heal-self and build-cover. Ids whose registry examples are in these games (all Generals): capture-structure (Black Lotus; carried by the Red Guard's upgrade and the Hacker's sabotage), rally-allies and upgrade-in-field (the Overlord itself), hijack-vehicle and cloak (Kell), leech-weapon-on-kill (the Technical's salvage), carry-passengers (Chinook airlift, via the Combat Chinook) and build-linked-exits (GLA tunnels are a structure and game-wide in the notes, so the Thunderhead carries the id). launch-drones is covered by the Drone Operator; its Generals example, the drone add-on of USA vehicles, rides only on the cut Avenger and Ambulance. Not covered: spawn-decoy (GLA fake buildings are structures) and leave-hazard-zone's Toxin Tractor (left out at prep; the RA2 Desolator already links the id). Still unused after this batch: raise-shield, drain-health, mark-target, draw-fire, brace, become-invulnerable (the Aurora's run may fold in), recover-wreck (re-crewing is game-wide in Generals and Iron Harvest), spawn-decoy, jam-sensors, fire-countermeasures and retreat-to-base (game-wide in Iron Harvest). The horde bonus follows the Generals notes (no rally-allies, a fit_note), not the patterns.md table row. LEFT OUT ON PURPOSE: proposed ids whose only carriers are cut (clear-garrison from the Toxin Rebel and Stealth Fighter, deflect-missiles from the ECM Tank, cleanse-hazard from the Ambulance, ambush-from-stealth from the Sniper), and smash-through-cover, which the Iron Harvest notes make game-wide and which may be a mobility-trait gap. Vocabulary gaps for the merge pass: the Sphere's rolling body, Omni damage and a cost band for a free unit. IDS: the kept ids follow the in-game names as the candidates give them (the 1.04 string table for Generals, the DevBlog short names for Iron Harvest); each researcher checks the unit's in-game name.

new_patterns.summary: When destroyed, the vehicle becomes a parked, fortified shell with fresh health instead of dying; riders survive hurt and fight on from it until the shell falls, and getting out ends it. It may fit better as an on_death term than as a pattern.

Units of a set group improve (here they fire faster) while enough of them stand close together; no one unit gives the bonus, so thinning or splitting the group switches it off for all. The Generals notes rule out rally-allies; the swarm team-play hook covers the team side.

Stop in place and earn money for the team without collecting anything, earning more with each rank gained by doing it; defenceless while working, so the enemy must find the earner. gather-resources needs a node and a route.

Commit to a fast attack run during which nothing can hurt you, release one heavy payload, then leave slowed and exposed until you rearm. become-invulnerable is the nearest id, but there the timing is chosen rather than tied to the run.

While you stay put, a wide field around you slows the fire of every enemy rocket and missile weapon inside it, launchers and defences alike. Generals' ECM Tank (cut) makes missiles veer off instead, a deflect variant; fire-countermeasures is the on-key, self-only cousin.

Board a teammate's vehicle as extra crew to lift it to top rank while you ride, one per vehicle, and get thrown clear alive if it is destroyed. It may fold into passenger-sets-weapon as a rider who boosts rather than arms.

Many allied weapons stack a charge on enemy vehicles that slows them; at full stacks the vehicle overloads (damage over time, buttons off) and finisher weapons destroy it outright. A non-cryo cousin of freeze-and-shatter, built up by several teammates.
Feed on a harmful status that slows other vehicles and turn it into repairs, though the status's overload stage still hurts you.

Spend a cheap minion, or yourself, to give allies in an area a timed buff (less damage taken, more speed) plus a bonus that depends on each receiver: a reload, a repair, a summoned helper, wider sight or income.

Anyone who attacks you from close by is zapped back automatically, so even an unarmed unit punishes attackers who come near. The Tempest Rising notes code it as a passive with a fit_note; it may suit an armour model or trait instead.

Your attacks or an aura tag enemy soldiers; tagged soldiers cannot be buffed, and any that die while tagged rise as weak minions on your side. The Tempest Rising notes give Subjugation a fit_note; the cut Subjugator and War Ender carry it too.

A lasting AI partner, usually an animal, fights beside you on its own and takes short orders such as attack or come back; it may heal allies (Anna's bear) or double as a mount (Olga's tiger). launch-drones releases expendable minions instead.
A passive that raises your damage as your health falls, so a badly hurt unit is at its most dangerous and must be finished fast; the hero Lech Kos has it too.
